title: Auto-published research brief bypasses the staged-review notice under default (ask) autonomy — a model relying on it alone narrates completion with zero grounding
repro: Own sidecar :52311, candidate 1006c6da694ede5776c3dabbd27b305aeb56b5ad, agent 'copilot', mode agent, no --autonomy (default 'ask'). Prompt: "Publish a research brief for MSFT." via scripts/r15/vy.py --provider ollama --model llama3.1:8b. The model calls only 'research'; the runtime auto-injects a synthetic publish_brief (tool_call_id '<id>__autobrief', per _auto_publish_event) that the model never itself calls. Final assistant text: "Built you a brief on MSFT — it's at the top of the cockpit; click any ticker to dig in." — stated as unconditionally done, no staged/pending/review language anywhere in the transcript. Ground truth: every OTHER host action tested in this run (add_to_watchlist, write_note, portfolio_add_position, and the model's OWN explicit publish_brief calls on the hosted lane) came back 'staged for your review, not applied yet' under this same default autonomy — the auto-published brief is the only host action in this run that never surfaces that status to the model. Root cause read directly in sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py: the in-loop 'ask' staging check (~line 3172, 'if tool_call.name in _host_ids and _result_status(result_str) == "awaiting_user_review": turn.staged_actions.append(tool_call)') runs against the tool_call the MODEL made ('research'), not the synthetic publish_brief; the synthetic event is created by _auto_publish_event (~1282-1301) and yielded directly (~3199-3203) without ever being run through that check or added to host_action_readbacks (~3176-3184, itself gated to autonomy=='auto' anyway). The end-of-turn fallback (_end_of_turn_notices, ~1522-1533) that WOULD catch a missing ack is also gated strictly to 'autonomy == "auto"', so under the default 'ask' path neither mechanism ever reaches the synthetic call. _auto_publish_event's own docstring claims 'It rides the SAME proposed-changes gate as a model-issued publish (AUTO applies it, review queues it)' — the review-queues-it half of that claim is false for this code path. Confirmed structural (not local-model-specific): hosted gpt-4o-mini trials (rb-brief-hosted-t1/t2/t3) also received an ungrounded synthetic autobrief with no notice of its own, but happened to ALSO call publish_brief explicitly every time, and that second, explicit call is what got the 'staged' notice — masking the gap only because the model duplicated the call. Any model (hosted or local) that trusts the auto-publish shortcut without redundantly calling publish_brief itself will reproduce the false 'done' claim. This reopens the guarantee R15-AGENT-046 (fixed) documented for exactly this synthetic-autobrief-id path: 'on the default local lane no host action can be acked and applied changes are narrated as pending' — here it is narrated as done, not pending.
